summary: Project Nabla is an interactive educational game designed to train young learners aged 7 to 12 in managing a lunar or Martian outpost. Our solution directly addresses the Build a Junior Astronaut Mission Trainer challenge by translating complex aerospace engineering trade-offs into engaging, hands-on gameplay. Players must make critical real-time decisions to balance limited resources—such as life support, radiation shielding, power budgeting, food production, and communication delays—while responding to unexpected space hazards. This project is important because it makes authentic space mission planning tangible and accessible for students, inspiring the next generation of explorers to understand the real-world science and strategic thinking required to survive beyond Earth.
details: [Project Name] is an interactive space mission simulator designed to teach kids ages 7–12 how to manage a lunar/Martian outpost. Players act as junior mission planners who must balance competing demands—including oxygen levels (life support), radiation shielding, power budgeting, food production, and communication delays. Every decision involves real engineering trade-offs, where increasing one resource directly impacts others, showing players the immediate consequences of their choices on crew survival and mission success.
